facts.statement: The study investigates how RNA-binding proteins contribute to the development of metabolic syndrome, a condition linked to diabetes and heart disease.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: Researchers used two models to study metabolic stress: treating hypothalamic cells with TNF-α and feeding mice a high-fat diet for either 8 or 12 weeks.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The proteins NOVA1 and hnRNP U changed the splicing patterns of specific genes, SNAP 25 and MDM2, as metabolic stress progressed over time.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: A strong effect of the protein hnRNP U on gene splicing was specifically observed in a type of diabetic mouse known as db/db.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: When the amount of hnRNP U was reduced in cells, it caused a specific gene splicing error, triggered cell death pathways, and reduced the cells' ability to take up glucose.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The authors suggest that these RNA-binding proteins could serve as early targets for future treatments of metabolic syndrome.
facts.subject: other
